subject: physics
question_text: Define root mean square speed of gas molecules.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 9 (printed p.137). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: v_rms = √(v̄²) = √((v₁² + v₂² + … + v_N²)/N) is the correct definition, used because the mean velocity of a gas at rest is zero while the mean square speed is not, matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The definition
lines: The root mean square speed is the

steps.margin_note: First mark. Say square root of the mean of the squares of the speeds — all three words matter.
steps.why: The molecules of a gas move with a whole range of speeds, so a single typical speed has to be built from all of them. Squaring gives extra weight to the faster molecules and ties the result to kinetic energy; the reason a mean is not taken over velocities is that velocity is a vector and averages to zero.
common_mistakes: Calling it the average speed. The average speed and the rms speed are different numbers.
Leaving out the words square and root — the name describes the exact three-step calculation.

recall.must_convey: That the root mean square speed is the square root of the mean of the squares of the speeds of all the molecules.
accept: square root of the mean of the squares of the speeds
square, mean, root of all the speeds
reject: mean velocity of the gas is zero
heard_as: square root of the mean of the squares

steps.memory_tip: Square each speed, take the mean, then take the root — that order is the name itself.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the formula and state why v_rms is used instead of the mean velocity.
steps.why: Velocity is a vector, so molecules moving in every direction cancel to a mean of zero even though they are all in motion. Squaring the speed before averaging removes the direction, so the mean square speed — and its square root, v_rms — is a genuinely useful non-zero number.
common_mistakes: Writing the average velocity formula instead of the mean of the squares of the speeds.
Missing the N in the denominator — it is a mean, not a bare sum.

recall.must_convey: That v rms equals the square root of the sum of the squares of all the speeds divided by N, and it is used because the mean velocity of a gas at rest is zero while the mean square speed is not.
accept: square root of sum of squares of speeds by N
mean velocity is zero but mean square speed is not
reject: square root of the mean of the squares of the speeds

steps.memory_tip: Mean velocity cancels to zero; mean square speed does not — that is why v_rms is used.

insider_note: State why v_rms is used, not just the formula — the reasoning about the mean velocity being zero is often what earns the second mark.
